newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union calls for action on civil servant pay.
newsitem.headline: French union calls for action on civil servant pay.

text.p: The French Communist-led CGT union called on Friday on other labour organisations to join in a week of action to press the government on talks on civil servants' pay, frozen last year.

"We renew our call for a meeting to examine the common initiatives that would allow a massive show of strength," the CGT secretary general for the civil service branch, Bernard Lhubert, wrote in a letter to his counterparts in other unions.
Public service minister Dominique Perben started on Thursday a round of union meetings, with a view to opening pay talks which had been promised by Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Perben yesterday met officials of the Force Ouvriere (FO), CGT and FSU unions, and is due to meet the CFDT and UNSA unions on Tuesday, and then the CGC and CFTC on Thursday.
The CGT said it wants a week of protests between January 27 and 31. It is calling for a 2,000 franc increase in monthly salaries, which some unions believe to be excessive.
"There will be no solution without an economic revitalisation brought about through an increase in purchasing power and development of stable employment," the CGT said.
The FO has not joined the call to action, preferring to wait for the next round of meetings in two weeks but it does want an element of recovery of income lost in 1996.
"We demand real negotiations for a catch-up for 1996 and a minimum of maintaining the standard of living in 1997 and 1998," the FO said in a statement.
Perben insisted on Thursday that budget constraints limited his room for manoeuvre on civil servants' pay but that he wanted an agreement on the issue.
The government froze public servants' pay last year and said it would negotiate salaries for 1997 and 1998. Most unions do not rule out a claw-back of the sacrifice made in 1996.
